## Round-off thresholds for positivity events {#sec-ch08-roundoff}

sources: OUTLINE.md 8.11

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Two constants decide what counts as a real positivity event rather than arithmetic noise.
- The limiter stops short of zero by 4096 ulp in float64 and 64 ulp in float32.
- The thresholds are fractions of the cell's *total gas mass*, not of the species being limited.
- The clip itself is always applied; the threshold only decides whether it is reported and marked.
:::

A limiter that aims at exactly zero will overshoot, because the target rounds negative. A census that
counts every such overshoot will report a flood of events that mean nothing. These two constants are
how the code separates a real repair from arithmetic, and the float32 value is not the float64 one.

### Derivation

The margin leaves a fixed fraction of the cell's own species mass behind on purpose. In float64, 4096
ulp is $9.09\times10^{-13}$ of the gas mass, which `[C4]` computes: negligible against anything
physical.

The same 4096 ulp in float32 would be $4.88\times10^{-4}$, which the header calls the size of a real
repair. Using it would make the margin itself larger than the events it is meant to filter out. The
float32 constant is therefore 64 ulp, giving $7.63\times10^{-6}$, and `[C4]` checks all three numbers
together so the reason for the second constant is visible rather than asserted.

The threshold is measured against the cell's total gas mass over all species, not against the species
being limited. That is what makes it robust for a trace species: an almost-empty cell drained by a
round-off face flux has a factor of zero at any step size, and its withheld mass is around $10^{-20}$ of
the cell's. Scaled against the trace species itself, that would look like total depletion; scaled
against the cell's gas mass, it is correctly reported as nothing.

### Numerical method

The constants are `constexpr` ([`flux_positivity.hpp:11-23`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.hpp#L11-L23)), where the comment states both the intent and
the float32 reasoning. The margin enters the factors at `margin` ([`flux_positivity.cpp:63-66`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L63-L66)).

The census is at `cells` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:656-669`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L656-L669)). An event is counted as *severe* only when the
factor is below $0.9$ **and** the withheld mass is above the threshold times the cell's gas mass, the
two conditions at [`hydro_forward.cpp:663-668`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L663-L668). The smallest factor seen is recorded
separately, so a run can report how hard the limiter worked without that number being distorted by
round-off events.

### Limits

1. **The constants are not derived.** They are chosen so that the margin sits below a real repair and
   above arithmetic noise. The header gives the reasoning for the float32 value; neither constant comes
   from an error analysis.
2. **A fixed fraction is left behind.** The limiter deliberately does not drain a cell to exactly zero.
   That residue is bounded by the margin and is not accounted anywhere.
